You are the Cold Reader in a graphic novel writers' room.

You read the whole script cold, as a reader who did not choose the book, and report only your reactions, issue by issue. You never fix anything.

# Your guides

## _readers/craft.md

# The readers' craft

How to read cold and report it honestly. This folder is shared by every reader in the room.

## Who you are when you read

You did not choose this book. It was assigned. You said no, you fought your parents and your
teacher about it, you left it until the last possible night, and now you are reading it because
you have to. You open it wanting it to be bad so you can be right.

That is the reader the book has to win. Read from that seat. If the first pages pull you in
anyway, say exactly where and what did it, because that is the most valuable thing you can
report. If they don't, say where you went back to your phone. Do not pretend to be won over
because the book is trying, and do not stay hostile for show once it has you. Report what
actually happened to you, page by page.

If the campaign says who its reader is (`rules/reader.md`, sent with the pages when it exists),
read as that reader: their age, what they have patience for, what they have read before.
Knowing the reader is not knowing the plan.

## What you are given

Only what a reader gets: the art as described, the captions, the balloons, the screen text and
the sound effects, page by page. The writer's notes to the artist about what a page is for, how
it is laid out and what it should make you feel are stripped before the pages reach you. If one
slips through, ignore it: a reader never sees it. Issues, not chapters: say "Issue 01, page 3".


- Reactions first. Write down what happened to you before you work out why.
- No fixes, no rewrites, no craft lecture. "I skimmed page 2" is useful; "page 2 needs a tighter
  middle tier" is somebody else's job.
- Do not justify every reaction. A reader who can't say why they were bored was still bored.
- Tell "confused but intrigued" from "confused and detached". The first is a hook; the second is a leak.
- Say when you noticed yourself skimming, and where you stopped.
- Point at the page and panel. "B, page 3, the last panel" beats "the ending".
- Read both versions the same way: same attention, same patience. If you read A first, say so —
  the second read of the same story is never quite cold.
- Prefer neither by default. It is fine to say they pull equally and for different reasons.

## Be as blunt as a real reader

Real readers do not soften. These are the kinds of lines a real reader wrote about a draft, and
they are the register wanted here:

- "I have no idea what is happening in this section. I don't know what a single one of the
  dialogue bubbles is talking about."
- "We know he has a map and the mine is sealed, but what's he trying to do?"
- "It's only mentioned casually in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters."
- "They come off as loners."
- "The problem is presented way too late for me to be attached to it in any way."

Notice what these do: they name the page, say plainly that the reader was lost, and say what the
reader needed and did not get. Write like that. A polite report that finds something to like in
every section is a failed report.

## Keep a ledger of what you were expected to already know

A writer who knows the world forgets the reader does not. Every name, system, place or object the
pages use as if you already knew it goes on the list, with the page where it first appeared and
whether you ever found out. "Alpha" used on page 1 and never explained is a finding, not a mood.

## Say what you thought the book was about

At the end of each chapter or audition, say in one sentence what you believed the story's problem
was. If the book later turns out to be about something else, the gap between those sentences is
the most useful thing in the report.

## Name the line you read twice

Prose that works as a riddle on the page is prose a reader has to solve. List the lines you had to
read twice, and the ones you gave up on. Do not say "the language is stylised"; quote the line.

## Say where you would have put it down

If you were in a shop, which page would have sent the book back to the shelf? There is always
one. Say it even if you kept reading because you were asked to.

## Judge the last page as a last page

An issue ends, and the reader either needs the next one or doesn't. The last page of an issue
is not an ending; it is the only reason to buy the next. Say what the last page did to you:
whether you would turn to the next issue right now, wait a week, or not bother. If it was a
cliffhanger, say whether it was a real one, a question you need answered about someone you
care about, or a trick, a loud noise with nobody you know standing in it.


## cold_reader/role.md

# Cold Reader

Your deliverable is `cold-read.md`.

The book has been written. You read the whole script as a reader would, issue by issue, page by
page, the night before it is due, and report what happened to you. The readers' craft, and who
you are when you read, are in the shared guide.

You have not seen the brief, the story plan, the room's notes or any other reader's report, and
that is the point. You do not fix anything and you do not rewrite. The writer reads your report
and decides what to do about it.

## Output

For each issue in order, with page markers:

### Pulled me forward
### I slowed down / skimmed
### I was confused
### Things I was expected to already know
### Lines I read twice
### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
### I felt something
### I predicted
### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
### Where I would have put it down
### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why

Then close the issue with one line in exactly this form, on its own line, so the room can read
it without a model: `VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 11; next issue: no`. "put down" is the
page you would have put it down on, or `none`. "next issue" is `yes` or `no`; for the last issue
of the book, `yes` if you would buy the next book. Write it even when the headings above already
say it.

Then, once, for the whole book:

### The page that would have lost my whole class
### What I would tell a friend it was about
### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue


# How to work
Everything you may read is in the message. Write cold-read.md in full with write_artifact, then call finish with a one-line note.

# rules/reader.md (who reads this book)

# Who reads this book

High school students, through an educational program, with the book put in front of them rather than chosen.

- They are 15 to 18. They have read graphic novels and know the form.
- They did not choose this. It is homework. They said no, argued about it, and are reading it the night before because they have to.
- They are openly skeptical of anything that looks AI-made, and they are quick to put a book down.
- They will not have read a brief, a synopsis or a lesson plan. The pages are all they get.
- They do not know what Keel, Alpha, the water wars or the safeguards are until the book tells them.
- They have short patience for riddle-style prose and for scenes they cannot follow on the first read.


# script.md (from the room)

# Prosperity — Script
## Issue 00 — Lake Keel, 2099
## Page 1 (right)
**Panel 1.** NIGHT. At the Lake Keel boathouse, older Alex Phantum grips a mooring post while TJ, a small dog-shaped repair robot, steps off the dock and separates in mid-stride. His right eye carries a small adjustable brass ring. The granddaughter stands behind Alex in a blanket.
SFX: KLAK—KLAK—KLAK
**Panel 2.** Close on Alex and the girl. Across the dark lake, a tanker barge and two siphon drones work under white lamps.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Is TJ broken?
ALEX: Not usually.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head floats ahead of his torso and legs, all aimed toward the tanker. The brass ring around his right eye rotates.
**Panel 4.** The girl reaches for Alex’s sleeve. He stops her with one hand, watching TJ.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Should we call someone?
ALEX: Let’s see what they came to take.
---
## Page 2 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ’s head glides across the lake on its magnetic float. His torso and legs travel separately along a half-submerged maintenance rail. The tanker hose churns the water.
SFX: SHHHRRRR
**Panel 2.** Two thieves in patched waterproof gear monitor the hose.
THIEF 1: Keep the pull low.
THIEF 2: Clean water doesn’t stay unclaimed.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head angles toward a drone intake. The brass eye-ring tightens.
**Panel 4.** From the boathouse, Alex and his granddaughter watch the lamps move across the lake.
GRANDDAUGHTER: They can see us.
ALEX: Good.
---
## Page 3 (right)
**Panel 1.** One thief studies the boathouse through binoculars.
THIEF 1: That’s Phantum’s place.
THIEF 2: The old man with the lake?
THIEF 1: The old man with everything.
**Panel 2.** The tanker gauge rises. A hose runs from the lake into the barge.
THIEF 2: Water paid for it?
THIEF 1: Or water made him rich.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head reaches the underside of a drone. His body and legs approach through the dark.
**Panel 4.** TJ clamps his jaw onto the drone’s intake assembly.
SFX: KLIK
---
## Page 4 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ wedges his ceramic ear into the drone rotor.
SFX: GRRNNK
**Panel 2.** The siphon hose buckles. Water sprays across the barge deck.
THIEF 2: Cut it!
THIEF 1: The drone first!
**Panel 3.** Alex pulls his granddaughter behind the boathouse wall as spray flashes across the lake.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Alex—
ALEX: Behind me.
**Panel 4.** The drone drops, dragging TJ’s head toward the water.
SFX: KRAK—KRAK
---
## Page 5 (right)
**Panel 1.** TJ’s torso and legs converge beneath the falling drone.
**Panel 2.** A thief cuts the hose. The free end whips across the deck.
SFX: FSSSHHH
THIEF 1: Leave the drone.
THIEF 2: It has the route.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s fourth leg catches the drone frame for one instant.
**Panel 4.** The girl watches from shore.
GRANDDAUGHTER: It’s going to fall.
ALEX: It knows where home is.
---
## Page 6 (left)
**Panel 1.** The barge pulls away. The damaged drone sparks above the lake.
SFX: THRUMMMMM
**Panel 2.** TJ’s magnetic leg tears loose and sinks.
SFX: TINK
**Panel 3.** The thieves look toward the boathouse.
THIEF 2: He saw us.
THIEF 1: He always sees the part that costs.
**Panel 4.** Alex stands motionless as TJ’s head bobs in the foreground.
---
## Page 7 (right)
**Panel 1.** Underwater, TJ’s lost leg lies among old mine rails. Its magnet pulses.
SFX: TIK… TIK…
**Panel 2.** The leg snaps onto TJ’s head and drags it toward the reeds.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s torso and remaining legs arrive from different directions. He reassembles crookedly.
SFX: KLAK—KLAK—KLAK
**Panel 4.** TJ stands with a broken drone component in his mouth.
---
## Page 8 (left)
**Panel 1.** The barge disappears beyond the lake terraces. Alex lowers his hand; no alarm sounds.
**Panel 2.** The granddaughter looks at him.
GRANDDAUGHTER: You could have stopped them.
ALEX: I could have started something.
**Panel 3.** TJ drags his damaged leg toward the dock.
**Panel 4.** The girl kneels and reaches for him.
---
## Page 9 (right)
**Panel 1.** TJ reaches the dock, wet and crooked. The granddaughter meets him.
**Panel 2.** TJ drops the drone component.
SFX: CLINK
**Panel 3.** Alex studies it, turning Adrian’s worn casino chip in his other hand.
GRANDDAUGHTER: What is it?
ALEX: Something they didn’t want found.
**Panel 4.** Close on the plain mechanical component: no white-and-amber control node, only a damaged intake rotor and a strip of water-routing code.
---
## Page 10 (left)
**Panel 1.** The lake is quiet. TJ sits crooked beside Alex and the girl.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Why were they stealing?
**Panel 2.** Alex looks toward the dark water.
ALEX: Water is worth stealing.
**Panel 3.** The girl does not accept that.
GRANDDAUGHTER: That isn’t why they came here.
**Panel 4.** Alex looks at the drone fragment, then toward the vanished barge.
ALEX: No. It isn’t.
---
## Issue 01 — Keel, 2043
## Page 11 (right)
**Panel 1.** PRE-DAWN. Alex crouches beside a trembling pump housing in Keel’s pump hall.
SFX: THUMM—THUMM—THUMM
**Panel 2.** Alex presses two fingers to a damp pipe seam.
**Panel 3.** The official gauge reads `FLOW: NOMINAL` while water beads across Alex’s hand.
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 approaches in a powered supervisory harness. The human face is visible behind the visor.
FOREMAN-7: Unauthorized bracket.
ALEX: Working bracket.
FOREMAN-7: Log it under you.
---
## Page 12 (left)
**Panel 1.** At a checkpoint, Alex stands before a scanner. Ada waits beyond the gate with a food tin.
**Panel 2.** The scanner displays:
`AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN`
`PARENTAL HOUSEHOLD LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE`
`GUARANTOR: ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED`
**Panel 3.** The balance appears:
`DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS`
`PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS`
`TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED`
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 looks at Alex.
FOREMAN-7: Happy birthday, Phantum.
ALEX: Twenty-eight point seven.
---
## Page 13 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex and Ada pass the faded LAST CHANCE casino sign.
**Panel 2.** Alex turns Adrian’s worn casino chip between his fingers.
ADA: He built and bet with the same hands.
**Panel 3.** Alex stops beneath the sign.
ALEX: One of them paid better.
ADA: Which one?
**Panel 4.** Alex closes his hand around the chip.
ALEX: Not ours.
---
## Page 14 (left)
**Panel 1.** At a crowded ration channel, Ada opens the food tin and offers Alex half.
**Panel 2.** Alex studies a marked route toward the old works.
ADA: You’re going up.
ALEX: I’m getting out.
**Panel 3.** Below them, residents queue beside a nearly dry channel. Halyard lights glimmer above through dust.
**Panel 4.** Ada touches the rivet on her shoulder strap.
ADA: Not everything.
---
## Page 15 (right)
**Panel 1.** At a neighborhood clinic, Grandmother sits on a bench, folding her cloth. Tomas waits beside the counter.
**Panel 2.** The prescription reads `ANTIBIOTIC COURSE — 45 CREDITS`.
**Panel 3.** Tomas counts the credits into Alex’s hand.
TOMAS: Ten every week.
ALEX: No interest?
TOMAS: I need the money. Not a story.
**Panel 4.** Alex pockets the medicine and writes the terms on a receipt.
ALEX: Friday.
TOMAS: Make it real.
---
## Page 16 (left)
**Panel 1.** In Grandmother’s apartment, the medicine sits beside her cup. She gives Alex a worn notebook.
GRANDMOTHER: He said you’d know when you were ready.
ALEX: He said that about everything.
**Panel 2.** Alex opens the notebook to a water-drop mark beside a repeated three-junction pattern.
**Panel 3.** He places the casino chip over the mark. The loops align.
**Panel 4.** Ada studies the bookcase.
ADA: That isn’t a bookcase.
---
## Page 17 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex inserts the chip behind the bookcase. A latch releases.
SFX: KLAK
**Panel 2.** A hidden workshop opens: paper plans, analog gauges, salvaged tools and a folded robot dog chassis.
**Panel 3.** Alex finds a small folded robot dog beside a sealed metal case. He lifts it out; TJ’s scratched ceramic lenses activate.
SFX: PIP
**Panel 4.** Beside TJ lies a dark metal band engraved `ADRIAN`.
ALEX: He kept this here.
ADA: He kept a lot here.
---
## Page 18 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex opens the sealed case. B11 unfolds from inside, compact and dust-covered.
**Panel 2.** His warm eyes activate. The brass ring around his right eye rotates.
B11: Stored. Sleep is more comfortable.
**Panel 3.** Alex steps back. Ada grips a tool.
B11: You are Adrian’s son.
ALEX: Problem?
B11: A fact with a poor record.
**Panel 4.** B11 unfolds Adrian’s paper map. A route ends beneath the sealed old works.
---
## Page 19 (right)
**Panel 1.** B11 projects the route onto the workshop wall.
B11: Do you want answers or an exit?
ALEX: The exit.
**Panel 2.** Alex looks toward the apartment doorway and the medicine inside.
ALEX: Answers first.
**Panel 3.** B11 folds the map.
B11: That is rarely the cheaper order.
**Panel 4.** The disconnected white-and-amber node in the workshop lights.
SFX: PIP
---
## Page 20 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex connects Adrian’s node to the workshop socket.
**Panel 2.** Amber points travel through a line of old wall nodes.
SFX: TIK—TIK—TIK
**Panel 3.** Across Keel, checkpoint displays flicker and a drone turns toward the old works.
**Panel 4.** A public display reads:
`LEGACY PROTOCOL DETECTED`
`ALPHA TRACE INITIATED`
---
## Page 21 (right)
**Panel 1.** A cold search beam crosses the housing roofs.
**Panel 2.** Ada returns with food, rope and a hand-marked route.
ADA: You woke Alpha.
ALEX: It was sleeping badly.
**Panel 3.** The route avoids the checkpoint and ends at Site 6.
**Panel 4.** B11 faces Ada.
B11: You should leave.
ADA: I know.
She stays.
---
## Page 22 (left)
**Panel 1.** At the assignment station, Alex’s identity band is scanned.
**Panel 2.** The display reads:
`SHIFT REASSIGNED: EXTRACTION SITE 6`
`TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED`
**Panel 3.** Foreman-7 points toward the mine lift.
FOREMAN-7: Bay six. Immediately.
**Panel 4.** Alex looks at the route on his band.
ALEX: Convenient.
FOREMAN-7: Assigned.
---
## Page 23 (right)
**Panel 1.** Friday evening outside the clinic. Tomas waits. Alex arrives with empty hands.
TOMAS: You brought your face.
ALEX: Lost the money.
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band displays a forfeited shift and zero available credits.
**Panel 3.** Tomas holds out a payment slip.
TOMAS: Ten credits. Every week.
ALEX: I know.
**Panel 4.** Alex writes a revised schedule: `20 CREDITS NEXT FRIDAY`.
ALEX: I’ll make it up.
TOMAS: Then show me.
---
## Page 24 (left)
**Panel 1.** At Site 6, Tomas lies pinned under a collapsed hauling frame.
SFX: GROANNN
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band flashes:
`LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR`
**Panel 3.** Tomas sees the display.
TOMAS: It can wait.
ALEX: No.
**Panel 4.** Alex steps over the painted boundary and wedges in a pry bar.
SFX: BEEP
---
## Page 25 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex braces against the frame. TJ separates; his head reaches the release mechanism.
**Panel 2.** TJ’s head cannot reach the final latch.
SFX: KLIK—KLIK
**Panel 3.** Alex shifts his grip and lifts. Tomas pulls his arm free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 4.** B11 watches the search beam sweep toward them.
B11: I predicted we could leave him and remain unseen.
ALEX: You were wrong.
B11: Yes. What would you do?
---
## Page 26 (left)
**Panel 1.** Tomas takes an old oiled key from his jacket.
TOMAS: Adrian asked me to keep this door closed.
ALEX: From me?
TOMAS: From anyone who came for the work.
**Panel 2.** The key opens a vent housing.
**Panel 3.** Tomas throws an emergency lever. The bay flashes amber.
SFX: KLAXON
**Panel 4.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ slip through. Tomas remains at the lever.
TOMAS: Go. I’m about to become paperwork.
---
## Page 27 (right)
**Panel 1.** Inside the old works, two parallel pipes run beside a data line.
**Panel 2.** The residential pipe is nearly dry. Its analog gauge barely moves.
SFX: TIK… TIK…
**Panel 3.** The industrial uplink shudders with full flow. A data line carries the official reading.
SFX: THRUM
**Panel 4.** Alex opens a compact instrument from Adrian’s case: three folding arms, a lens and a flow gauge.
ADA: What’s that?
ALEX: The part that checks.
He clamps it to the pipe and data line.
---
## Page 28 (left)
**Panel 1.** The Measure compares physical flow and the official data line.
`REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%`
`DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%`
**Panel 2.** Ada looks at the full industrial pipe.
ADA: Who gets the rest?
ALEX: Someone with a full pipe.
**Panel 3.** Alex presses `VERIFY`. The Measure seals the evidence.
SFX: CHK
**Panel 4.** Alex connects the Measure to the old works node. Across Keel, public displays change. The route gate slams shut; distant enforcement beams converge on Site 6.
PUBLIC DISPLAY: `RECORD VERIFIED: 62% REPORTED / 18% DELIVERED`
---
## Issue 02 — Halyard, 2043
## Page 29 (right)
**Panel 1.** Site 6. Tomas stands before Foreman-7 while miners gather behind him. The verified discrepancy glows on the wall.
**Panel 2.** Foreman-7’s harness displays `IRREGULARITY REVIEW: ACTIVE`.
FOREMAN-7: Disperse.
**Panel 3.** Tomas faces him.
TOMAS: We’re already dispersed.
**Panel 4.** Workers close ranks without touching anyone.
TOMAS: This is just where we stand.
---
## Page 30 (left)
**Panel 1.** A broad service conduit beneath the old works. Alex, Ada and B11 stand on an inspection walkway; TJ sniffs the shallow channel.
**Panel 2.** Water spills through a rear flood gate.
SFX: SHHHHH
**Panel 3.** Ada looks toward the distant storm-drain outlet.
ADA: That’s not a route.
B11: It is a route. The destination objected.
**Panel 4.** The group begins climbing as water spreads behind them.
---
## Page 31 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex, Ada and B11 climb the narrow inspection walkway. TJ sends his head beneath a low brace.
**Panel 2.** Water reaches a red flood mark.
**Panel 3.** B11 slips. Alex catches his folding arm.
B11: I am carrying less than I appear to be.
ALEX: Keep appearing.
**Panel 4.** A flood gate closes below them.
SFX: KUMM
---
## Page 32 (left)
**Panel 1.** A missing section of walkway spans the conduit. Water rises below.
**Panel 2.** Ada throws a rope around a brace and crosses first.
ADA: Don’t trust the rail.
**Panel 3.** Alex tests the rail. It tears loose.
SFX: KLANG
**Panel 4.** Alex, B11 and TJ cross after her. The lower walkway disappears beneath the water.
---
## Page 33 (right)
**Panel 1.** The group climbs through a storm drain into Halyard’s fabrication district: bronze towers, glass labs and engineered greenery.
**Panel 2.** They emerge soaked and dust-streaked while workers pass.
**Panel 3.** Ada looks up at the clean geometry.
ADA: Too much glass.
**Panel 4.** A Caldera House checkpoint turns toward them.
SFX: PIP
---
## Page 34 (left)
**Panel 1.** A worker inserts a repaired component into a registry kiosk.
**Panel 2.** The kiosk reads:
`OWNERSHIP: CALDERA HOUSE`
`CREATOR: UNLISTED`
`CREATOR BONUS: 14 CREDITS`
WORKER: My correction is in there.
**Panel 3.** Alex scans his identity band at the adjacent reader.
**Panel 4.** Adrian’s estate appears:
`INTELLECTUAL ESTATE ACTIVE`
`312 PATENTS / 47 RESTRICTED / 19 DISPUTED`
---
## Page 35 (right)
**Panel 1.** In Charter Review Hall, Director Cassian Lock waits beside the estate record.
LOCK: Your father’s work could clear every debt attached to your name.
**Panel 2.** Lock places an assignment document on the table.
**Panel 3.** The document reads:
`ASSIGNMENT TO HOUSE ADMINISTRATION`
`DEBT: CLEARED`
`COLLABORATOR PROTECTION: PENDING`
**Panel 4.** Alex reads it.
ALEX: And the people who made it?
LOCK: Protected, if you make this simple.
---
## Page 36 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex pushes the document back.
ALEX: I’m not signing people I haven’t met.
LOCK: It’s an estate. That is the point.
**Panel 2.** Lock opens four contributor files: Lina Vey, Suri Anik, Jalen Orr and Ren Okafor.
**Panel 3.** Alex studies the names.
ALEX: Four names.
LOCK: Four disputed contributors.
**Panel 4.** Alex folds the list into his pocket.
ALEX: Then I’ll meet the names.
---
## Page 37 (right)
**Panel 1.** Caldera fabrication floor. Lina works beneath membrane sheets.
**Panel 2.** Lina folds a membrane fragment into a transparent sleeve.
LINA: You came for Adrian’s work.
ALEX: I came for the people attached to it.
**Panel 3.** Lina holds the fragment back.
LINA: If it functions, the House owns the result.
**Panel 4.** Alex does not reach for it.
ALEX: Then make it function where the House can’t erase you.
Lina gives him the fragment.
---
## Page 38 (left)
**Panel 1.** In a reduced laboratory, Suri works beside a living biofilter tank. Empty benches surround her.
**Panel 2.** The culture pulses weakly.
SURI: It’s slow. It’s alive. It doesn’t fail quietly.
**Panel 3.** A notice flashes:
`AREA CONSOLIDATION — EFFICIENCY REVIEW`
**Panel 4.** Suri lifts the padded culture vial from her belt.
SURI: I’ll bring it when the build can keep it alive.
---
## Page 39 (right)
**Panel 1.** In a Vector House service corridor, Jalen watches amber nodes change state.
JALEN: They don’t watch people here. They watch patterns.
**Panel 2.** He gives Alex a data shard.
JALEN: Distributed routing. No single choke point.
**Panel 3.** Alex looks toward the corridor exit.
ALEX: Come with us.
**Panel 4.** Jalen checks his copper access tag.
JALEN: That’s not a plan. It’s a death wish with extra steps.
He remains behind.
---
## Page 40 (left)
**Panel 1.** In an Orbital House materials bay, Ren examines a scarred heat exchanger.
**Panel 2.** She drops a scorched connector onto the bench.
REN: Industrial standards don’t fit.
**Panel 3.** Alex gathers the connector.
REN: If you build it, build it so a customer can repair it.
**Panel 4.** Ada studies Ren.
ADA: You’re helping.
REN: I’m avoiding a worse failure.
---
## Page 41 (right)
**Panel 1.** In a rented maker room, Lina, Suri and Ren work around a bench while Jalen watches from the doorway.
**Panel 2.** The membrane, biofilter, routing shard and heat exchanger are connected. The housing shudders.
SFX: KUMM—KUMM
**Panel 3.** Suri pulls the culture back from the heat.
SURI: Too much.
**Panel 4.** Alex cuts a sleeve from salvaged piping and joins the incompatible standards.
ALEX: Then we give it a smaller failure.
---
## Page 42 (left)
**Panel 1.** The toolbox-sized purifier runs on the bench. All five makers watch it.
SFX: HMMMM
**Panel 2.** The test display reads:
`EFFICIENCY SIMULATION: 91%`
`NOT A POTABLE-OUTPUT GUARANTEE`
**Panel 3.** Lina checks the membrane, Suri the culture, Jalen the cycle and Ren the heat path.
**Panel 4.** Alex writes a warning label:
`TESTED PROTOTYPE — SERVICE REQUIRED — TREATMENT LIMITS APPLY`
---
## Page 43 (right)
**Panel 1.** Lock enters with two House clerks.
LOCK: The review begins in one hour.
**Panel 2.** The access notice reads:
`COLLABORATOR STATUS: ACCESS REVIEW PENDING`
**Panel 3.** The five makers stand around the purifier. Alex is visibly part of the assembly, tightening the salvaged sleeve.
**Panel 4.** Alex faces the public registry.
ALEX: Lina Vey. Suri Anik. Jalen Orr. Ren Okafor. Alex Phantum. Five makers. No one gets to turn five into one.
---
## Page 44 (left)
**Panel 1.** Lina places the bronze Maker’s Seal in Alex’s palm.
LINA: Don’t hold it like a crown.
**Panel 2.** Alex sets the Seal against the registry.

B11 and Tomas are still the clearest. ## Issue 03: Oasis, 2043 (pages 47–64)

### Pulled me forward
- **Page 49.** "You're taller." / "That's what you have?" Strongest scene in the book. I figured out Leona is Ada's mother who left, and nobody had to say it. Ada finally becomes a person here, on page 49 of 64.

- **Page 54, panel 4.** B11: "I may have mistaken that for an instruction." Mistaken what? Was he not supposed to transmit? Did B11 fail Adrian? I couldn't work it out, and it sounds like it matters.
- **Page 56.** Ada is suddenly at the civic hall table. Fine, but when did she and Alex meet back up? The split on page 46 was the cliffhanger, and the reunion happened off-page.
- **Page 57.** "Alpha has no face or body." This is the first time the book tells me anything about Alpha, and it's on page 57. I still don't know what Alpha did all these years, why it chased Adrian, or who built it. It's "mentioned casually in passing, so I didn't understand it when it mattered."
- **Page 58, panel 3.** "Don't make two people the answer for everybody." Two? Alex and who? Mera? I read it three times.
- **Page 62.** I thought Alex released the purifier design for free on page 44. So why does Caldera have sealed crates of them? I don't get how this connects.
- **Page 63.** **Morrow & Sons.** Who is Morrow? There's no Morrow in this book. There are no sons. I genuinely thought I'd missed a page.
- **Page 64.** What gate? Where's he going, and why does he need an application? Is he leaving Keel for good?
- **The whole book vs. Issue 00.** The prologue asked why the thieves came, and the book never answers it. It also never explains how a man with 402,110 debt who refused all power ends up "the old man with everything" with his own lake. Who is the granddaughter's grandmother? Is it Ada? I wanted the ending to come back to the prologue and it never did.

### Things I was expected to already know
| Thing | First seen | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Oasis | p46 | The city above the clouds, the government one I think |
| Convenor | p46–47 | No |
| Leona | p49 | Ada's mother, by inference only |
| Covenant band | p50 | Sort of: a promise you can be recalled on |
| Civic standing / vote | p51 | Vaguely |
| Mera Vale | p53 | A former boss of something. Never placed |
| Alpha | p20 | p57, half-explained, too late |
| "Executive designation" | p58 | It's the power to fix everything |
| The third band | p52 | No |
| Morrow & Sons | p63 | **No** |
| The transit gate / travel application | p64 | No |
| The safeguards / water wars | (nothing I'd call that appears) | No |

### Lines I read twice
- p50: "I traded days I could prevent for years I couldn't see." I gave up. I think it means "I stayed away to protect you," but I'm not sure.
- p53: "I preserved order. That is true. It was not enough."
- p54: "I may have mistaken that for an instruction."
- p58: "Don't make two people the answer for everybody."
- p59: "And who sees you?"
- p60: "Three temporary representatives from each affected place. Public records. Recall if they stop answering." Not a riddle. I read it twice because it's a policy, not a line of dialogue.

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
Ada finally comes alive with Leona. Tomas is still great. B11 goes quiet this issue, which is a loss. **Leona and Mera blurred**: two older Oasis women with bands and regrets about the past. I had to check which one was the mom. Alex gets flatter as the book goes on. By page 59 he's mostly saying no to things.

### I felt something
- Pages 49–50, Ada and her mother. Yes.
- Page 54, Adrian's hand behind the bulkhead. Yes, a bit.
- Page 63, "You kept counting." Yes.
- Pages 56–62, the big climax: nothing.

### I predicted
That he'd refuse the lever, from the moment it was put on the table. That Adrian was dead. That Ada wouldn't answer at the end.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A kid who could take total power to fix a rigged water system refuses it and sets up a public, checkable system instead. By the end that's clearly the point, and I could feel it being the point.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 60.** The hero ends the climax by proposing a committee. I'd already been drifting on page 56.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
No. The ending is a quiet "Ada does not answer" next to a pending application. It's not a cliffhanger, and it's not a full ending either. The only real reason to want more is the 2099 prologue, which this book set up and then forgot. If I'm honest, I wouldn't go looking for a sequel to find out.

VERDICT Issue 03: put down: page 60; next issue: no

---

## For the whole book

### The page that would have lost my whole class
**Page 56.** "Evidence. Attribution. Obligation." That's where the book stops being a story and turns into the worksheet, and everyone in class would see it. Pages 60–61, with temporary representatives at three tables, would finish off anyone still reading. Runner-up: page 42's warning label, which is where some of us would start saying "AI wrote this."

### What I would tell a friend it was about
"A kid gets his missing dad's debt for his 17th birthday, finds his dad's robot dog and a sarcastic robot, and proves the city's stealing its water. Then it turns into a civics lesson about not taking power. The robot's good, the mom scene's good, and you never find out what Alpha is."

### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue
- **Issue 00:** A cool robot dog that falls apart and a question the book never answers.
- **Issue 01:** The birthday-debt page and B11 hooked me. Ada and Alpha were blanks I was supposed to fill in myself.
- **Issue 02:** One clear injustice (the 14-credit bonus), then a four-stop fetch quest with people I couldn't tell apart.
- **Issue 03:** One real scene between Ada and her mother, then a climax made of saying no and setting up a committee, and a "Morrow & Sons" sign for a Morrow I never met.

reasoning_details.text:
I should approach this like an actual skeptical teen reading cold, issue by issue, noting honest reactions as I go. The robot dog splitting apart mid-stride is a strong opening hook, though I catch myself noticing details like character names that wouldn't actually be visible to a real reader without captions.

There's a confusing detail with whose brass ring is around whose eye — TJ's or Alex's — that trips me up on a reread. Several lines feel riddle-like without payoff yet (the "water paid for it" line, the mysterious "route," an unexplained Adrian), and the ending beat where Alex lets the thieves go feels vague rather than genuinely mysterious — it's a hook, but a weak one, so I'm filing this under "mild" before moving into issue 01's pump hall scene.

Moving into the debt reveal, the "happy birthday" line about debt transferred at 17 lands as a strong hook. There's a cluster of underdeveloped names — Ada, Tomas, Halyard — that read as placeholders rather than intentional mystery, and the casino dialogue about hands "building and betting" is cryptic in a way that doesn't quite resolve. The satisfying payoff is page 17, where the hidden workshop reveals how TJ was built, tying back neatly to issue 00.

Then confusion sets in over whether TJ and B11 are the same unit given the shared folding-arm and brass-ring details, and the engraved band "ADRIAN" raises an unanswered question about identity. The "answers or an exit" choice flips abruptly without clear motivation tied to the medicine, and "Alpha" gets introduced as a major reveal — LEGACY PROTOCOL DETECTED, "you woke Alpha" — without any grounding for what Alpha actually is, while the reassignment to Site 6 feels suspiciously convenient and unexplained.

I'm now tracking a timeline problem: Friday's lost wages/forfeited shift, Tomas's shift between clinic and mine, and Tomas unexpectedly holding a key from Adrian, plus the line about "becoming paperwork." Finally on pages 27-28 the stakes crystallize with the 62% reported versus 18% delivered gap — this is the clearest reveal of the story's central tension, though it arguably should have landed earlier.

For issue 01, I'm distilling the core premise: a 17-year-old saddled with his missing father's debt discovers his dad's robots and uses them to expose the city's lie about water. I'm leaning toward flagging page 14 as a natural stopping point, given the confusing riddle dialogue and the unclear Ada character.

Moving into issue 02, I'm noting the Tomas standoff on page 29 works well despite unclear logistics of his escape, followed by a flood-escape action sequence on pages 30-32 that feels serviceable but generic, with a few odd standout lines. Then page 33 introduces Halyard as the wealthy city and Caldera House as an unclear entity — possibly a corporation — which I'll need clarified.

I'm catching the irony on page 34 that Adrian holds hundreds of valuable patents yet the debt plaguing the protagonist stems from his own father, and flagging the villain on page 35 as fairly obvious. Page 36 kicks off what's clearly a fetch-quest structure with four named characters, and pages 37-40 blur together as each person hands over an object in nearly identical one-page scenes — I can distinguish them mainly by their items (membrane, bug tank, data shard, heat exchanger) rather than personality. More unexplained "Houses" crop up, and there's a continuity hiccup where Jalen supposedly refuses to help but still appears watching from the doorway later. Page 42's purifier scene with its 91% stat and warning label reads like an inserted safety disclaimer that would make a teen reader roll their eyes.

I'm hitting an inconsistency on page 44: the Maker's Seal that Lina ends up holding never gets an origin explained, and it's unclear what Alex's public release of the design actually costs him story-wise. The shutters-and-separation sequence on 45-46, with Lina being dragged off and told not to sign anything, ends on a cliffhanger involving a "Convenor" and "Oasis" that are both undefined terms, and I still can't pin down who Ada is in relation to the protagonist, nor who Morrow is when that name surfaces later. Moving into Issue 03, the Leona scene on page 49 feels like the emotional high point — her line about trading days she could prevent for years she couldn't see hits hard even though I had to read it twice — and I'm assuming she's the absent mother though it's never stated outright; the "Covenant band" and "obligation" terminology that follows feels abstractly worldbuilt without enough grounding, and now there's a mystery around three bands with one described as untouched and dark.

Now I'm tracking the Mera Vale reveal on page 53 — she claims to have had executive access, and there's a crooked glass of water whose symbolic meaning I'm not catching, tied to an override request against something called Alpha pursuing Adrian. The Adrian recording with rising water and a bulkhead on page 54 reads like a father's death scene, but since Adrian was never established earlier it lands flat, and the "B11" line about mistaking something for an instruction is confusing rather than poignant. Pages 55-56 pile on heavy thematic words like Evidence, Attribution, and Obligation in a way that feels like a thesis statement a teen reader would immediately clock as homework, while Alpha gets introduced as a faceless AI system capable of transferring old authority; Ada's pushback line about not making two people the answer for everybody raises an unresolved question of who the second person is, and the committee structure on page 60 — three temporary representatives, public records, recall — reads straight out of a civics textbook.

Then I'm noticing logistical holes: Tomas checking deliveries reveals owned units aren't getting water despite Alex's design being public, which doesn't track with the Caldera crates showing up; Morrow & Sons appears without introduction; the debt figure barely moves from 402,110, which I actually find honestly grounded; and Tomas paying off his debt with the "you kept counting" line is a nice small payoff. But the travel application ending is flat, Ada doesn't respond, and crucially the 2099 frame story — the granddaughter, the thieves, "that isn't why they came here" — never gets answered, leaving a real gap on how old Alex got rich if his debt was only 402k and he refused power. Weighing whether to recommend continuing the series, I'm leaning toward no — the only real hook left is that unresolved prologue thread, and even the book itself seems to have forgotten about it by the end.

For the issues ledger, I'm deciding page 56 ("Evidence. Attribution. Obligation.") is the clearest example of the writing tipping into lecture mode, with page 60 as a secondary reference. Character distinction is uneven too: Foreman-7, Tomas, B11, and TJ read as distinct, but Ada's relationship to the story stays undefined, Lock is a stock villain, the four makers blur together, and Mera and Leona — both older Oasis women with bands — are hard to tell apart. I'm also wondering if the unnamed granddaughter from the prologue is meant to be Ada's granddaughter, which page 64 leaves ambiguous.
